test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following synthetic chemicals was responsible for the sharp drop in the amount of ozone in the atmosphere in the 1980s?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorofluorocarbons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):**
 
• CFCs are synthetic chemicals that were widely used as refrigerants, propellants in aerosol cans, and in various industrial applications.
 
• When CFCs are released into the atmosphere, they eventually reach the stratosphere, where the ozone layer is located.
 
• In the stratosphere, ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun breaks down CFC molecules, releasing chlorine atoms.
 
• Chlorine atoms act as catalysts, destroying ozone molecules in a chain reaction.
 
• This process led to a significant depletion of the ozone layer, particularly the formation of the "ozone hole" over Antarctica in the 1980s.
 
• CFCs are very stable molecules, which means they can remain in the atmosphere for long periods of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroiodocarbons:**
 
• While iodine can also contribute to ozone depletion, chloroiodocarbons were not as widely used as CFCs.
 
• The primary driver of ozone depletion in the 1980s was the widespread use of CFCs.
 
• Iodine compounds tend to be less stable in the lower atmosphere, and therefore less likely to reach the stratosphere.
 
• The primary chemical of concern was chlorine.
 
• Iodine containing chemicals have different reactions than chlorine containing chemicals.
 
• **Iodobromocarbons:**
 
• Similar to chloroiodocarbons, iodobromocarbons were not the primary cause of the ozone depletion observed in the 1980s.
 
• Bromine, like chlorine, can also destroy ozone, but CFCs were the dominant ozone-depleting substances.
 
• Bromine is also a very efficient destroyer of ozone.
 
• The concentration of bromine containing chemicals was not as high as Chlorine containing chemicals.
 
• The Montreal protocol addressed bromine containing chemicals as well as chlorine containing chemicals.
 
• **Iodofluorocarbons:**
 
• While these compounds exist, they were not the main culprits behind the ozone depletion of the 1980s.
 
• The stability and widespread use of CFCs made them the primary concern.
 
• Fluorine itself does not directly destroy ozone in the same way that chlorine and bromine do.
 
• Iodine compounds are less stable in the atmosphere.
 
• The combination of Chlorine and Fluorine in the CFC molecule created a very stable compound that was very damaging to the ozone layer.
